Issued at 322 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Currently...

Been another dry, but breezy day across the forecast area  
today...and outside of a narrow swath of lower-level stratus 
gradually creeping E-SE with time, more of the area has seen
more sun. Looking at the upper air pattern today...seeing 
sharper southwesterly flow spreading across the Plains...set up 
between gradually eastward shifting ridging to our east and a 
shortwave disturbance currently shown through the Nrn Rockies 
into the central High Plains. Further west...another, stronger 
upper level low pressure system is working its way onto the 
northern half of the West Coast. As this Nrn Rockies upper level
disturbance continues to swing ENE further onto the Plains, an 
accompanying surface frontal boundary is making its way through 
the forecast area...roughly about halfway through by mid-
afternoon. Ahead of the front, gusty southwesterly winds have 
continued, gusting near 30 MPH at times...behind the front, a 
switch to gusty west-northwesterly winds. This front is also 
ushering in a quick drop in dewpoints and thus relative humidity
values...no changes made to the Red Flag Warning currently in 
effect through 6PM today across our WNWrn counties, where the 
best opportunity for the gusty winds/low RH for at least 3hrs 
remains. Doesn't look to be any big surprises with temperatures,
with most spots topping out in the mid-60s. A few models 
continue to hint at the potential for at least some sprinkles 
during the late afternoon hours as that frontal boundary pushes 
east...but without much other model support, decided to keep any
precip mention out.

Tonight through Friday...

This upper level disturbance will continue to push mainly
through he Dakotas tonight, ending up over the MN/Can border 
by sunrise Thursday. The accompanying surface front is expected 
to diminish/wash out as it loses its upper level push...with the
weaker sfc pattern bringing light and at times variable winds 
this evening through the overnight hours. While much lower 
dewpoints will have worked their way into the NWrn half of the 
forecast area...that push doesn't look to get all the way 
through, keeping some lower level moisture around...and with the
light winds and little sky cover, models continue to show the 
potential for the development of fog as we get closer to sunrise
Thursday into the mid-morning hours. Best potential for fog 
(visibilities under 1 mile are possible) looks to be roughly 
along/south of a line Geneva, NE to Phillipsburg, KS.

Outside of that fog/lower level stratus potential into the
morning hours, overall Thursday doesn't look to be too bad of 
a day...and honestly looks to be the nicest day of this 7-day 
forecast period. Expecting generally partly cloudy skies...with 
winds turning back to the south as sfc low pressure starts to 
reorganized ahead of the next approaching upper level system, 
speeds for much of the area look to top out around 10-15 MPH, 
though the WSWrn half could have afternoon gusts closer to 20 
MPH. Highs look to reach right around 60 in the NW to mid-60s in
the SW.

Dry conditions are forecast to continue on into Friday, but the 
winds will be cranking back up. Overall, hasn't been any notable
changes in models...after a bit of a lull, stronger 
southwesterly flow aloft returns, as that system currently 
moving onto the West Coast pushes further inland. By the end of 
the day on Friday, models aren't in too bad of agreement, 
showing the main upper level low over the western half of 
Canada, with troughing extend southward through the Rockies into
western portions of the Desert SW. While the forecast remains 
dry with this system still off to the west...surface low 
pressure will continue to deepen as the system approaches, 
bringing increasing southerly winds to the entire forecast area.
Sustained speeds in the 25-30 MPH range are not out of the 
question, along with the potential for gusts exceeding 40 MPH. 
So although forecast high temps are a touch warmer than Thursday
with more mid-upper 60s, the winds will make for a less 
pleasant day. 

This weekend into next week... 

During the weekend through Monday time frame...any precipitation 
chances in the forecast remaining focused on the Saturday-
Saturday night time frame. Models aren't in too bad of agreement
looking at the big picture in the upper levels...showing that 
above mentioned troughing continuing to work its way east 
through the Rockies and onto the High Plains through the first 
half of the day Saturday...though there are still some 
differences with finer details like the timing and exact 
location of precipitation. A swath of precip running from the 
Srn Plains up into the western Great Lakes looks to develop by 
early afternoon, as large scale lift increases between the 
shortwave troughing emerging from the Central/Srn Rockies and
